help:
usage: gnd verify [-h] [--sidecar SIDECAR] [--artifacts ARTIFACTS]
                  [--no-extraction] [--out OUT] [--format {text,json}]
                  model population

Run the full derived verifier: popvalidate then check over a PRE-EXTRACTED
population file. This command never calls a model and never orchestrates
extraction (R-03''): the executing agent running the gnd-extract skill writes
the population and its <population>.extraction.json sidecar, and verify
validates the handoff before composing the checker. Exit bands are REUSED
unchanged with precedence 3 > 1 > 4 > 2 > 0: 3 ill-formed (including an ill-
formed extraction handoff), 1 alethic fail, 4 indeterminate, 2 vacuous, 0
pass. The payload's extraction block carries the machine-readable state (ran |
skipped | failed + reason); a missing sidecar is extraction:sidecar-missing, a
malformed one extraction:sidecar-invalid, and a digest that does not match the
file bytes extraction:binding-mismatch — all exit 3, state failed. skipped is
written ONLY by --no-extraction. Never a fidelity rate in this payload: a
checker pass over an uncalibrated extraction is checker acceptance, not proof
of faithfulness.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model file
  population            path to the PRE-EXTRACTED population file (YAML or
                        JSON)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --sidecar SIDECAR     path to the extraction sidecar (default: the
                        population path with an .extraction.json suffix,
                        beside the population)
  --artifacts ARTIFACTS
                        directory containing the model's extraction bundle;
                        required on the extraction path so projection_sha256
                        is verified
  --no-extraction       the INTENTIONAL opt-out: check a population that was
                        not produced by an extraction; records
                        extraction.state=skipped with the reason
  --out OUT             also write the JSON payload to this path (from argv
                        only)
  --format {text,json}  output rendering: human-readable text (default) or one
                        JSON payload
